Beikdugang (Beikdugang, Y15)

Region (English scoring-table region): Haless.

In one sentence: Turn a Halessi trading port into a free republic spanning the oceans, lighting a maritime revolution with fleets, global trade, and technological exchange.

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Long (62 direct Y15 missions) | Mission-tree update: local support for EU4 v1.37.5.0; the official 2026 remake log is design context only | Uniqueness: Very high | Grind: Medium-high (oceanic distance, trade partners, and revolutionary prerequisites) | Early pressure: Medium | Expansion: High, mainly coastal and overseas

Not a freedom beacon from nowhere

In 1444 Beikdugang is already a Jiangyang-culture merchant republic, using the Merchant Reform, with Beikdugang as its capital. Its history file also records an old enmity with Tianlou, an anti-eunuch flag, and the scholar-ruler Wang Ji. It begins as a local power with a trade tradition, not as a maritime empire that already owns a global revolutionary fleet. Early mission text says that it has long envied Tianlou's control of the Yanshen advantages; the land and sea routes controlled by its rival are the old order Beikdugang must prove it can break.【Local history script】【Local flavour text】

Poetry and nautical writing repeatedly turn their gaze beyond the horizon. Beikdugang is meant to leave its Halessi port and open trade and diplomacy with the Lake Federation in the north, Aelantir, and more distant coasts. The missions do not merely grant naval combat bonuses: they require real routes, ports, markets, ships, and partner relationships. Oceanic distance, explorable waters, and a trade network are its threshold; a player who fights only on land around the Yanshen will miss its clearest content.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

The offline Wiki has no independent country-history page for Beikdugang, but the Treasure Fleet entry preserves an earlier port clue: Zurkanreki merchants expelled by Tianlou came here, and the Treasure Fleet used the port for nautical supplies, maps, and cargo. This explains why Beikdugang treats overseas contact as an opportunity, but it cannot establish the republic's founding year, every generation of rulers, or the complete extent of its 1444 trade. The early merchant origin and the current Merchant Reform echo each other, but each source has its own boundary.【Wiki source】【Local history script】

Trade partners and the republic

The Lake Federation is an important partner in the mission tree. Beikdugang trades relics with it, establishes transoceanic routes, and even studies its constitution when considering restraints on its own polity. Some missions redefine “subjects” as equal partners of a maritime empire, explicitly arguing that personal rights should not be reserved for citizens of the homeland. This shows the transition from a merchant-interest state to a state of political ideals; those ideals still require diplomacy, institutions, and port construction, and a declaration alone does not prove equal status in every colony.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

The mid-game economy runs through Sarhal, Insyaa, and Aelantir. The relic market brings profit and makes intercontinental knowledge-sharing possible; later missions propose supplying some relics to international artificer research rather than locking them in the national treasury. Beikdugang is therefore simultaneously a port, an explorer, and a technological intermediary. Its challenge to Tianlou on land runs alongside overseas cooperation, and the campaign map grows larger as the time needed to prepare fleets and secure supplies grows with it.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

Revolution after the northern lights

The mission future presents the northern ice sea, straits, and aurora as an explorable route, then enters a global revolutionary narrative: ideas travel by ship, and peoples beyond Haless enter the imagination of freedom and rights. Beikdugang seeks to spread enlightenment, build allies, and support maritime action. Its union with the Lake Federation is more than a trade agreement and may become a deeper military partnership in the mission text. Global revolution is a late political ambition, not an established fact in 1444; actual improvement of rights in each region still depends on local mission and event effects.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

The final artificer and fleet route raises the technological threshold again. Cooperation with kobolds, gnomes, and dwarves leads toward metal hulls and steam power, and the text explicitly says that steamship construction and maintenance are very expensive; these are not free ships available at the start. Official Dev Diary 105 introduces the 2026 remake and its wider Sarhal, Insyaa, market, artificer, and revolutionary lines; this article uses it as design context only, while current playability remains governed by the local missions cited above.【Local flavour text】【Official development log】

Beikdugang's long campaign therefore expands twice: first from a local port into an ocean-spanning network, then from a trade network into a political platform where allies debate rights and institutions. Whether relics exist only for profit, whether distant subjects can be partners, and whether technology is shared all become questions the mission text asks the country to answer. The player still has to prepare shipyards, routes, and diplomacy by hand; ideals cannot replace a fleet. This is why older players describe it as both grand and easily delayed by prerequisites.【Local flavour text】【Community view】

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 79/100 | Authoritarianism 28/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 19/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 73/100) | Pluralism 87/100. Phase change: merchant port and Lake Federation trade (Expansion 54, magic-artifice intensity 35) → global revolution and steam fleet (Expansion 86, magic-artifice intensity 73).

The v2.1 value is Good (79/100), with an improving trajectory. Constitutional restraints, equal-partner ideas for subjects, international knowledge-sharing, and the spread of rights have positive evidence; exporting a global revolution may involve coercion, so restraint is lower than the other dimensions. A declaration is not proof that every colony has implemented rights. Conquest of Tianlou and overseas expansion are not treated as moral evidence by themselves. Players who like maritime trade, long routes, Lake Federation diplomacy, and a revolutionary-artifice blend will fit well; players who want quiet development in one region and dislike overseas supply and intercontinental prerequisites should avoid it.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

Older players greatly enjoyed Beikdugang's nautical and aurora stories, while also reporting that some missions depended on Lake Federation progress and random events. Because the mission tree was later remade, old posts describe historical experience only and cannot prove that the same bottlenecks remain in the current version.【Community view】

The version boundaries for the offline Wiki, official remake log, and community discussion are recorded in the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces native English national-idea names and descriptions alongside the inherited source displays. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Successor ideas do not stack automatically with the predecessor set. Descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal, not events already completed in 1444. Native English prose is used rather than back-translating the Chinese localisation; any inherited display/unit uncertainty remains unresolved.

Beikdugang (Y15) — Beikdugang Ideas

Traditions: Beikdugang Traditions

Effects: Global sailors modifier: +20%; Ship trade power: +20%.

Idea 1: Strangers in a Strange Land

Our ancient forefathers came from the great trade fleets of the north, who stayed here and built our fair city with their bare hands. We are still seen as outsiders by many, and are far more open to new ideas that have been rejected by the rest of Yanshen for their radicality and strangeness.

Effects: Idea cost: -10%.

Idea 2: Northern Trade

They come by every decade or so, mighty ships of the north with flags featuring the great rising sun of our ancestor's homeland. We remain one of their primary destinations, and benefit greatly from their honored patronage.

Effects: Trade efficiency: +15%.

Idea 3: Dajunshi

Driven away by the war ravaging their homeland during the Daehonse Period, countless Gowon refugees flocked to our shores soon after the plot against Jaher succeeded, assisting us in defending against Tianlou in the aftermath. They have since settled into our city, building their own slice of home, Dajunshi, on her outskirts.

As well as bringing an exotic and lush culture to our people, their mastery with the bow and arrow has proved a powerful asset to our armies.

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +10%.

Idea 4: Ships of the Violet Dawn

Our ships have always been legendary in these lands, based on the vessels of our progenitors and renowned for their durability and ease of maintenance.

Effects: Light ship cost: -10%; Sea repair: yes.

Idea 5: Fields of Forts

The hills north of Beikdugang are pockmarked with old and decaying fortifications built by a succession of conquerors and petty lords, we have a ready supply of material to pull from to repair our active bastions.

Effects: Fort maintenance: -15%.

Idea 6: Paradise of Zhuhan

The city our forebears hailed from is known as Zhuhan to our people. While all of Yanshen marvels in the mystery and splendor of its treasure fleets, it holds a special place in our hearts. Rumoured to be a gleaming city of amber and jewels, where even the poorest citizen dresses in linens of silk and gold, we are proud to claim such distinguished heritage.

Effects: Prestige decay: -1%.

Idea 7: Nanxin Naval Academy

Our naval officer academy is one of the most prestigious in Yanshen, and frequently collaborates with the Abosrekodh academy back in Zhuhan. The gifted sailors and admirals that graduate from Nanxin are a powerful boon to our navy.

Effects: Naval tradition: +1.

Ambition: Beikdugang Ambition

Effects: Naval leader manoeuvre: +1.
